correctness.rationale: I reconstructed Φ70 as Φ35(−X), propagated the linear functional on powers using its scalar characteristic recurrence, and confirmed the sixteen positive entries at 19..34, all other entries through 53 zero, and the entry at 54 equal to −2. After shifting off the smallest occupied exponent, positivity eliminates exactly the middle block. Reduction modulo Φ70 identifies X^35 with −1, and the two remaining block polynomials have degree at most 18<24, so are equal. This argument works over R and does not assume integer coefficients or infer real divisibility from a single complex root. The 19 antipodal generators have disjoint supports and give the claimed simplicial cone; the converse follows from the binomial and degree bound. Independently convolving the stated quotient with Φ70 gives the exact 16-term W. Its degree is 54 and its coefficients in degrees 0 and 35 differ, precluding binomial divisibility. evidence: Proof §1 identifies the rational signed CRT kernel with cᵢⱼ=uᵢ+vⱼ. Its rational equations extend over R (tensor the rational polynomial remainder map with R). At support diameter at most 53 subtract all overlapping antipodal pairs, leaving at most one root per signed cell. The net matrix is then cᵢⱼ=uᵢ−sⱼ. For any level t between two of its finitely many potentials, the matrix 1{uᵢ>t}−1{sⱼ>t} is additive, has entries 0 or ±1, and every nonzero sign is a matching sign of cᵢⱼ. If c≠0, at least one such cut is nonzero.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: That cut represents a nonempty squarefree vanishing subset supported in the residual interval. A minimal vanishing subset inside it cannot be an antipodal pair; the regular 5- and 7-gons have respective circular diameters 56 and 60. It must therefore be nonpolygonal with diameter at least 54 by the indexed theorem, a contradiction. Hence only antipodal pairs remain in 0..53, giving the 19-ray cone immediately. The indexed checkerboard W attains 54 and has no antipodal pair. This uses the kernel and actual bound, not merely the apparent similarity of statements.

evidence: The indexed 2pq theorem gives minimal circular diameter (2p−1)(q−1) for nonpolygonal minimal subsets. A subset of the normalized fixed interval 0..D has circular diameter at most D; to use attainment in the linear formulation, rotate a shortest covering arc to start at 0.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The two diameter conventions yield the same minimum after allowing shifts. The squarefree condition is an actual scope difference and requires the signed-kernel reduction below, rather than identification by numerical cutoff alone.
